{
  "findings": [

      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields but is used for audit logs",
      "body": "OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), but AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style key/value handling or must not be used for datetime columns."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 182,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Negative offsets are now passed to Django QuerySet slicing",
      "body": "BasePaginator now uses cursor.offset unchanged for previous-page cursors, and OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows negative offsets when advanced features are enabled. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices, so a crafted cursor with a negative offset can raise an exception instead of returning a page. Negative offsets should be rejected or normalized before slicing."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 197,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Span buffer switches from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration or key namespacing",
      "body": "Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code calls ZADD on those keys and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. If any in-flight segment from the old version exists during deployment, Redis will return WRONGTYPE and processing will fail, causing stuck or dropped spans. A new key prefix, migration, or drain procedure is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "ZPOPMIN eviction can remove root spans or other semantically important spans",
      "body": "The script caps each segment at 1000 members by removing the lowest-scored members, where score is end_timestamp_precise. It has no special protection for the segment/root span. If the root span has one of the lowest end timestamps, or a missing/zero timestamp, it can be evicted. The segment may then be marked as having a root span while the root payload is missing, breaking downstream segment semantics."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Redirect resolution depth was reduced to 1000 and can fragment deep traces",
      "body": "The loop follows at most 1000 redirects in the span redirect map. If a redirect chain is longer, the script stops at an intermediate set and stores the span there, which can prevent related spans from being joined into one segment. The previous limit was 10000 and the correctness tradeoff was at least documented; the new lower limit changes behavior for deep traces without tests or migration notes."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 174,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "SpansBuffer.__reduce__ reconstructs the object with the wrong positional arguments",
      "body": "__reduce__ returns SpansBuffer with (assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, redis_ttl). The fourth positional argument of SpansBuffer.__init__ is segment_page_size, not redis_ttl, and max_segment_bytes/max_segment_spans/redis_ttl are not preserved. When SpansBuffer is pickled for multiprocessing, the unpickled buffer will have incorrect configuration."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 449,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Flush path no longer enforces a span-count limit",
      "body": "_load_segment_data removed the check that skipped segments larger than max_segment_spans. The Lua script only evicts when new inserts push a set above 1000 members, so pre-existing or otherwise unevicted segments can contain many small spans under max_segment_bytes and be loaded, serialized, and produced in one flush, causing memory/CPU spikes or oversized downstream messages."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 105,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Typo assigning queryset.query.order_b leaves ordering unchanged",
      "body": "In build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently dropped, which can produce incorrect previous-page results for paginators relying on this branch."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py",
      "line": 157,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover the new eviction cap or set-to-zset migration behavior",
      "body": "The test changes only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures. There are no tests that insert more than 1000 spans to verify ZPOPMIN eviction, verify that root spans are preserved, or verify behavior when old Redis set keys exist. Given the data-loss and compatibility risks introduced by this PR, these cases need coverage."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields but is used for audit logs
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), but AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style key/value handling or must not be used for datetime columns.

findings.title: Negative offsets are now passed to Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: BasePaginator now uses cursor.offset unchanged for previous-page cursors, and OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows negative offsets when advanced features are enabled. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices, so a crafted cursor with a negative offset can raise an exception instead of returning a page. Negative offsets should be rejected or normalized before slicing.

findings.title: Span buffer switches from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration or key namespacing
findings.body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code calls ZADD on those keys and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. If any in-flight segment from the old version exists during deployment, Redis will return WRONGTYPE and processing will fail, causing stuck or dropped spans. A new key prefix, migration, or drain procedure is needed.

findings.title: ZPOPMIN eviction can remove root spans or other semantically important spans
findings.body: The script caps each segment at 1000 members by removing the lowest-scored members, where score is end_timestamp_precise. It has no special protection for the segment/root span. If the root span has one of the lowest end timestamps, or a missing/zero timestamp, it can be evicted. The segment may then be marked as having a root span while the root payload is missing, breaking downstream segment semantics.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth was reduced to 1000 and can fragment deep traces
findings.body: The loop follows at most 1000 redirects in the span redirect map. If a redirect chain is longer, the script stops at an intermediate set and stores the span there, which can prevent related spans from being joined into one segment. The previous limit was 10000 and the correctness tradeoff was at least documented; the new lower limit changes behavior for deep traces without tests or migration notes.

findings.title: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ reconstructs the object with the wrong positional arguments
findings.body: __reduce__ returns SpansBuffer with (assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, redis_ttl). The fourth positional argument of SpansBuffer.__init__ is segment_page_size, not redis_ttl, and max_segment_bytes/max_segment_spans/redis_ttl are not preserved. When SpansBuffer is pickled for multiprocessing, the unpickled buffer will have incorrect configuration.

findings.title: Flush path no longer enforces a span-count limit
findings.body: _load_segment_data removed the check that skipped segments larger than max_segment_spans. The Lua script only evicts when new inserts push a set above 1000 members, so pre-existing or otherwise unevicted segments can contain many small spans under max_segment_bytes and be loaded, serialized, and produced in one flush, causing memory/CPU spikes or oversized downstream messages.

findings.title: Typo assigning queryset.query.order_b leaves ordering unchanged
findings.body: In build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently dropped, which can produce incorrect previous-page results for paginators relying on this branch.

findings.title: No tests cover the new eviction cap or set-to-zset migration behavior
findings.body: The test changes only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures. There are no tests that insert more than 1000 spans to verify ZPOPMIN eviction, verify that root spans are preserved, or verify behavior when old Redis set keys exist. Given the data-loss and compatibility risks introduced by this PR, these cases need coverage.
